thread:
Maya: Quick thread  proposing a lightweight RFC: introduce 'stability buckets' (green/yellow/red) for catalog onboarding + a short/long pin escrow flow. Aim: stop noisy churn while giving customers visibility and test lanes. Thoughts?

Arjun: Sounds promising. How do buckets map to pins and to our migration automation? Need concrete mapping in the spec.

Priya: From eval team: suggest we derive buckets from three signals: normalized token entropy, response divergence (BLEU/Jaccard proxy), and a confidence CI on eval metrics. Map to a 0..1 composite score then thresholds.

Zoe: Product needs: green -> standard 14d auto-unpin, yellow -> enforced 30d short escrow with mandatory canary before swap, red -> block unless manual exception. Also require customers to opt into long escrow (90d) for enterprise.

Ben: CS asks for a 'test cohort' opt-in so customers can route 10% of traffic to a new model during escrow. That way they can verify before committing. Also need rollback request button in Console.

Maya: Spec sketch:
- Composite_score = 0.5*entropy_norm + 0.3*divergence_norm + 0.2*(1 - metric_ci). Lower composite_score better.
- Buckets: green <=0.35, yellow 0.35-0.6, red >0.6.
- Pin mapping: green -> pin_ttl default 14d, yellow -> pin_ttl 30d + mandatory canary (5%) for 72h, red -> blocked unless manual override.
- Enterprise flag: `pin_escrow: enterprise` enables 90d opt-in; requires contract flag and legal hook.

Arjun: API changes: add catalog metadata fields: `composite_score`, `stability_bucket`, `pin_ttl_days`, `pin_escrow` (enum: none, enterprise), `escrow_cohort_percentage`. Keep POST/PUT backwards compatible (optional fields). We'll add a migration job to backfill composite_score for existing models.

Priya: Eval infra: nightly job calculates components, emits CSV row per model+cohort with fields: model, cohort, composite_score, entropy, divergence, metric_ci, ts. Add `--stability-buckets` flag to the eval CLI to control thresholds. We'll also output a short human-readable one-line reason for the assigned bucket.

Zoe: UX notes: model detail page shows bucket, days remaining, escrow cohort percent, and a link to request manual override. Onboarding modal should explain why a model landed in yellow/red with actionable steps (add more prompts, tighten dataset, or request exception).

Ben: Ops constraints: long escrows and enterprise pins create capacity reservations. We need quotas per-customer and a global cap on enterprise-reserved GPUs. Also, enforce canary budget with Autoscaler so canary traffic won't exceed reserved headroom.

Maya: Migration UX: for existing pinned models, run backfill, then email customers with a short summary: current bucket, days left, and next eval date. Offer a one-click opt-in to enterprise escrow if contract allows.

Arjun: Rollout plan: feature-flag the bucket assignment and Console UI. Stage 1: internal-only for 2 weeks. Stage 2: opt-in customers and selected enterprise accounts. Stage 3: default on for new model in 6 weeks. We'll keep auto-migrate disabled behind flag until we've validated canary behavior.

Priya: Monitoring: add daily alerts for bucket-shifts (green->yellow or yellow->red) with root-cause link to the eval CSV. Also track false-positive denial rate (how often customers ask for manual exceptions after being blocked).

Ben: Runbook: on yellow->red alert: initiate quick eval, notify owner, create 5% canary if owner approves, require perf gates. If canary fails, rollback and mark model as unstable. If owner requests manual override, record reason and TTL.

Maya: Open questions: exact numeric thresholds (pilot suggests the ones above but need validation), legal language for enterprise escrow, and how to price enterprise pin add-on. Action items: @Arjun draft API + backfill job, @Priya add CSV + alerting, @Zoe mock Console copy and override UX, @Ben define quota enforcement + runbook. We'll review in product sync Thurs and push a pilot to internal users next week.

Arjun: I'll open the API PR today and include a migration plan.

Priya: I'll add the bucket export to nightly eval and run it against last 30 days for calibrations.

Zoe: I'll draft explanatory copy and a compact FAQ for customers.

Ben: I'll prototype quota checks and Autoscaler guard rails this afternoon.
